title: image/copy: progress bar reports inflated transfer rate
body:
`podman push / pull` users report invalid and unrealistic transfer speeds, e.g. 350 MiB/s to 1.1 GiB/s on a 20 Mbps link. This is an upstream report of https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/20634  

 ## Cause
Progress bars in [image/copy/progress_bars.go](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/blob/main/image/copy/progress_bars.go) use `decor.EwmaSpeed`, which `mpb` consumes in `(*mpb.Bar).ProxyReader` ([copy/blob.go](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/blob/main/image/copy/blob.go#L45)). That proxy reader measures only the time spent inside `Read()`. 
Ref: https://github.com/vbauerster/mpb/blob/master/proxyreader.go#L52

During a copy the bottleneck could be the consumer (registry socket / local disk), which stalls between reads. So the measured rate reflects the source read speed, not the actual transfer speed leading to inflated values coz if short bursts of `Read()`. In general, pull operations doesn't encounter this often coz network speed is usually lower than the local storage speed.

 ## Reproduction
Just push any large image to a remote registry that doesn't have it cached (with network being the throttle). Can also look at the comments on the downstream issue for many user reports reproducing it.
